newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRANCE'S TAPIE IN HOSPITAL AFTER HEART PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE'S TAPIE IN HOSPITAL AFTER HEART PROBLEM.

text.p: French failed tycoon and ex-soccer boss Bernard Tapie was rushed to hospital overnight after suffering a mild heart problem, emergency workers said on Wednesday.
Tapie, jailed nearly four months ago for fixing a soccer match and currently on trial for embezzling money from his former Marseille soccer club, woke up during the night complaining of chest pains.
But his illness might simply be due to stress from the trial, the emergency workers said.

The 54-year-old rags-to-riches businessman, who had pursued a promising career as a politician before ending up in jail as bankrupt prisoner 265 449G, was in hospital in Aix-en-Provence, southern France.
He is on trial on charges of embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) from the Marseille team.

He was jailed after the French supreme court upheld his eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
Nineteen other soccer figures are standing trial along with Tapie in the Marseille case, which opened on May 12 and is expected to last another two weeks.
He faces a five-year sentence if convicted on the charges of swindling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents between 1987 and 1993.
